name: Fluid Glass
rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; a single raw-WebGL fragment shader replaces the three.js scene, so the lens, bar and cube modes ship dependency-free within budget.

mode.description: Glass shape; unknown values fall back to lens.

size.description: Lens radius (half height for bar and cube), in px; capped to fit the host.

refraction.description: How strongly the glass magnifies and bends the backdrop.

followPointer.description: Steer the glass with the pointer; otherwise it only drifts.

speed.description: Time scale of the drift and backdrop motion.

a11y: The WebGL canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none; the host's own text and controls stay in DOM order above it and are never copied.
The backdrop stays dark (under 60% of the accent colours) so light text on the card keeps its contrast wherever the glass passes.
Reduced motion stops the render loop and draws one still frame with the glass centred; the CSS stand-in stops drifting too.
Without WebGL or script a static CSS gradient and glass shape stand in, and forced-colors mode hides the decoration entirely.
